turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Pain in my throat/tonsil area—sharp, like a knife stroke, about 7 out of 10—and it improves when I lean forward.
Can you tell me when this throat pain started and whether it began suddenly or gradually?
I don’t know. The pain seems to come on at a fast pace—about 9 out of 10.
Do you have any fever, chills, or feeling unusually warm today?
I don’t know.
Are you having trouble swallowing (odynophagia or dysphagia) or does anything make the pain worse, such as eating, drinking, or talking?
Yes. I have difficulty swallowing, or a feeling of discomfort/blockage when swallowing.
Do you notice any swelling, redness, or pus on one side of your tonsils or the back of your throat, or does the pain feel more localized to one side?
I don’t know. The pain involves both tonsils (R and L) along with the back of my neck, palate, and pharynx.
Do you have any neck stiffness, headache, or a sensation of pressure behind your eyes that’s getting worse when you lie flat?
I don’t know.
Have you had any recent upper‑respiratory symptoms (cough, sore throat, runny nose) or a recent illness such as a cold or flu in the past week?
I don’t know.
Are you experiencing any changes in your voice (e.g., sounding “muffled” or “hot‑potato”), drooling, or difficulty breathing that makes you feel like you can’t get enough air?
Yes. I have noticed that my voice has become deeper, softer, or hoarse. I also produce more saliva than usual.
Do you have a measured fever (temperature ≥ 38 °C/100.4 °F) or have you felt unusually warm or chills today?
I don’t know.

I don’t know.
